name: Tavian Achebe-Müller
description: Tavian Achebe-Müller built his career on a neural signature described by critics as 'structured cold' — a precise, almost architectural emotional restraint that audiences found paradoxically intimate. He worked exclusively in licensed Vantablack productions for eleven years before vanishing from public record in 2215 following his involvement in a controversial neural-feed project that was pulled from distribution six hours after launch. His current whereabouts are unknown.
cultural_impact: His disappearance became the defining example of what Shelf communities call 'the pull' — the moment a creative career is erased rather than ended.
story_hooks: A fragment of the pulled neural-feed has surfaced in a dead drop, and multiple parties want it — Vantablack to destroy it, journalists to publish it, and someone else for reasons that aren't clear.
Achebe-Müller is alive and hiding in the Shelf, trying to finish the project on his own terms using black-market BCI equipment.
A fan who experienced the six-hour release before the pull claims the neural-feed left a persistent emotional imprint she can't shake — and it's starting to affect her behavior.
